hypothesis.statement: The unchanged SP500 fresh15 v3 route can produce attributable future-only long and short lifecycle evidence under its frozen entry, exit, cost, and one-position-per-symbol contract.
hypothesis.update: The first post-boundary eligible setup was an additional short while the pre-boundary SP500 short remained open. It was intentionally withheld and did not create a lifecycle.

classification.watcher_state_interpretation: One post-boundary eligible evaluation exists without a new attributable lifecycle; it must not be credited to either side's lifecycle minimum.

technical_validation.router_contract: An eligible intent matching the currently open side is withheld as same_direction_position_open. An eligible opposite-side intent routes a close before any later re-entry.

current_followup_observation.interpretation: This point-in-time open mark is operational context only. It is mutable, is not a realized result, and cannot select an exit policy.

decision.recommendation: Keep V58 execution unchanged and continue the frozen future-only SP500 collector.
decision.why_now: The first post-boundary eligible setup is causally explained by portfolio occupancy and supplies no new lifecycle or exit-policy outcome.
decision.evidence_reviewed: Exact cohort routing row, frozen experiment preregistration, current route status, current V58 config, router source and tests, and one point-in-time checkpoint snapshot.
decision.observed_problem_or_opportunity: The route generated another valid short while the symbol was already short. The portfolio correctly refused to pyramid. The experiment still lacks a post-boundary attributable entry on either side.
decision.applicable_market_regime: Only the exact SP500 fresh15 v3 short setup at 2026-08-20T20:00:00Z; no broader regime or profitability inference is supported.
decision.alternatives_considered: Treat the setup as a missing trade, permit pyramiding, credit it as a lifecycle, modify the exit, or preserve the frozen one-position contract. The first three contradict the recorded routing and experiment contract; changing the exit is unsupported by this event.
decision.expected_upside: Continued collection can produce clean, non-overlapping long and short lifecycle evidence without contaminating sizing or exit-policy inference.
decision.main_risks_and_failure_modes: Sparse cadence may delay evidence; repeated same-side signals can remain occupied rather than attributable; the open lifecycle may resolve before a new entry; one or two outcomes can be winner-dependent; source or checkpoint gaps can censor a lifecycle.
decision.validation_completed: Exact route identity, prospective cutoff, signal readiness, router action/withholding counts, withholding reason, occupied side, protective stop, and report-only authority.
decision.validation_still_required: At least one post-boundary attributable and fully resolved lifecycle per configured side with exact fills, fees, funding, slippage, stop, exit, and matching profit-lock evidence.
decision.success_metrics: One fully resolved future-only long and one fully resolved future-only short for diagnosis; this remains a diagnostic minimum rather than a promotion threshold.
decision.failure_or_update_triggers: A later exact ledger row shows an action or order for this same sequence, the occupied side was not short at decision time, duplicate same-symbol exposure occurred, the source record changes, or future resolved evidence contradicts the frozen contract.
decision.confidence_level: High on routing and occupancy classification; low on route profitability and exit-policy value because no new lifecycle occurred.

single_highest_value_next_investigation.primary: Reconcile the existing SP500 lifecycle through its configured close, including exact exit reason, fill, fees, funding, slippage, stop behavior, MFE, MAE, peak giveback, and 100/40/80 profit-lock state.
single_highest_value_next_investigation.after_primary: Capture the first post-boundary attributable SP500 lifecycle on each configured side without relaxing entry, occupancy, sizing, or exit rules.
single_highest_value_next_investigation.reason: The open lifecycle currently contains the largest marked-to-stop giveback in the portfolio, while the future-only experiment still has zero attributable entries.

limitations: This record describes one eligible short setup and no new lifecycle, fill, realized PnL, or exit-policy outcome.
The point-in-time checkpoint mark and giveback are mutable operational context and cannot be reproduced from the replace-in-place checkpoint after it advances.
The raw routing record proves the withhold reason, but it does not estimate the counterfactual PnL of pyramiding or exiting.
Repeated same-side setup cadence is not independent trade frequency under one-position-per-symbol routing.
Zero long evidence and zero post-boundary attributable entries prevent side-breadth, profitability, or promotion claims.
No strategy, route, asset, entry, exit, leverage, sizing, risk limit, live config, order, stop, backend, or TUI process changed.
falsifier: Invalidate this classification if the exact routing record changes, if an action or order is causally attributable to sequence 290472, if no same-side SP500 position existed at that decision, if duplicate same-symbol exposure was created, or if the active route/config identity differs from the frozen identity. Update the economic disposition only after fully resolved future-only long and short lifecycles with exact costs and exit evidence.
